final.label: state-ownership-and-key-granularity

skill_entry.name: 14. One site owns a published record, every call into a gated subsystem sits under its gate, a cumulative row key names the same thread in every forward
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, in h/tron hunks. (a) A published record (a struct folded, printed or exported as one unit: stats row, counter record, FUSE leaf) gets fields from two layers, each writer filling fields the other never writes, or a begin/end pair in one function plus a time stamp around its call. (b) A direct call into a subsystem whose *_configure or *_reset sits under a guard the new site does not share, or a callback loop replaced by a direct call. (c) A cumulative table (never resized per forward) sized by one count (num_workers()) and indexed by a variable offset by a per-forward value (n_attn_workers). (d) A class or budget decided by one predicate over a whole forward.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Writers: keep atomic writes to a record member; drop locals and fold readers. Grep qualified members at HEAD; table member, writer, file, layer. 2. Callers: finding when a production caller reaches one writer and not the other, or one writer reads state only the other sets; a writer inside the other's caller on every path clears it. 3. Gates: the guard above the configure call and above every call into the namespace; unconfigured behaviour; exclude the diff's own switch. 4. Tables: size versus index, exposed versus fillable rows, fold bounds, leaf names. 5. Predicates: pre-review body validation tool, compute_forward_args for mixed forwards, per-element key at the counting site, README bucket definition. 6. One finding per record, subsystem, table, predicate.
skill_entry.question: Who owns this record, and does every caller, every model shape and every forward with a different worker split fill it the same way, so that a reader of the leaves sees one thread per row, one class per forward and no half records?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A record owned through a scoped object (forward_scope). A single-site counter with a reset (PR 2980 drew only an atomics question, 3406007619). A value one function moves between instances of one structure under a Note or TRON_ASSERT (subtree_pins tron-2875, kv_section tron-4353, both silent). A table resized every forward (ready_kv_plan). A function the body declares inert naming the follow-up PR (tron-2693). A call site already under the shared gate helper. A row key documented stable per thread (pool worker index). A per-forward class stated deliberate with the README naming the limitation (ae8a6d38d9). A clear partner with zero callers: dead-symbol check (3029165954). A gate or key spelled two ways: duplicate-logic check (3029194687, 4147010638). Tests driving inner hooks: 4125033677. Missing tests, formatting, wording.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Two layers write `<record>`: <fields> come from `<site A>` while <fields> come from `<site B>`. Any other caller of `<inner call>` (another scheduler, a test harness, a draft path) gives `<field> == 0` next to nonzero `<field>`. Consider owning <X> inside `<one function>`, or wrap <begin/end/stamp> in one scoped helper, so a single site owns the record. Key or class form: Design question on <row sizing | the forward classification>. Rows are sized by `<count A>` but indexed by `<index B>`, so <consequences as bullets>. Was keying by <B> deliberate? Keying by <A> would <benefit>. Alternatively, record `<n>` per forward so readers can interpret the rows. Gate form: endorse the finding, name the mechanism keeping every call under the guard.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal. The two-writer case is a statement that ends in 'Consider ...' with two options; his review summary called it one of 'A few correctness and semantics issues inline'. The key and class cases open with 'Design question on ...' and end in a question with two alternatives plus a documentation fallback ('If per-forward is intended, can the README spell out ...'). The gate case is an endorsement of a bot: 'good point... we should be consistent'. 'Nit:' never inside this check (the row-key-computed-two-ways nit 4147010638 belongs to the duplicate-logic check). Never blocking.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, full file (the record struct and its hooks), callers (git grep at HEAD for the inner and outer call), other files (the scheduler's compute_forward_args, the configure site, the Note on worker placement), PR body (the version that precedes the review: the sample run's n_workers and active_workers, the validation tool), runtime behaviour (how one forward gathers users is readable from h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp compute_forward_args; mark Insufficient data only for a scheduler outside full.hpp).

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: one owner per published record, one gate per subsystem, one stable key per cumulative row

Setup note: for a merged PR `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself (PR 4596: 1430736b2a). Use `BASE=$(for c in $(git -C WT rev-list --first-parent origin/main); do git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor $c HEAD && echo $c && break; done)` and confirm BASE against the baseline id the PR body names. Layers: h/tron/scheduler = scheduler, h/tron/models = model, src/tron/kernels = kernel.

1. Writers (a): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*(fetch_add|inc_relaxed|max_relaxed|\.store\(|\|= ))' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+.*(out|s|json) \+='`. Keep the `@@` headers to map each hit to its HEAD line (new-side hunk start plus offset). Keep only hits whose left side is a member access of a record struct (`x.member`, `x->member`, a bare member inside the struct's own member function); drop locals, string builds and fold readers (`out +=`, `visits[pass][p] += load_relaxed(...)`, `results[i].store(`). For each kept record take the struct name and its instance, then grep qualified, never a bare member name another struct or a scheduler variable also uses: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(INSTANCE|ARRAY\[[^]]*\])\.(M1|M2|M3)' HEAD -- h src`. Enclosing function: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<=L && /^  [a-z][a-z_0-9<>:& ]* [a-z_0-9]+\(/ && !/^  (if|for|while|switch|return)\b/ {f=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "f}'`. Table: member, writer function, file, layer. Two layers, or an inner function in one layer with the time stamp taken in another, make the record a candidate; step 2 decides whether it is a finding.

2. Callers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'state\.forward\(|\.run_forward\(|begin_forward\(|end_forward\(|note_forward_wall\(' HEAD -- h src t` (replace with the PR's hooks and the function that calls them). The candidate is a finding only when a production caller reaches one writer and not the other, or when one writer reads state only the other sets: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'current_class'`. A second writer that runs inside the first writer's caller on every production path clears the candidate (split_sections_by_query inside finish_sw_plan, model.hpp:2785 at a9a9cf30a4ac). Test callers are excluded (4125033677). One production caller at HEAD is not a clearance: name the future callers (another scheduler, a test harness, a draft path).

3. Gates (b): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(if constexpr|getenv\(|_enabled\(\)|_configured\(\)|_configure\()'`. Exclude the switch of the diff's own feature (an env_enabled() or getenv of the variable the PR introduces); a gate counts only when a configure or reset call of a subsystem the diff calls into sits under it. Guard above the configure call: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<L && /if constexpr|if \(/ {g=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "g}'`. Every call into the subsystem: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'tron::hardware::gof_[a-z_]+\(' HEAD -- h src`, same awk per hit. Unconfigured behaviour: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/tron/gof.cpp | grep -n -E '/ gof_n_layers|% gof_n_layers|gof_n_layers = 0'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'gof_max_layers()' HEAD -- h src`.

4. Row keys (c): size expressions `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(attn\.size\(\)|num_workers\(\)|std::vector<[a-z_]+>\(N_)'`. Confirm the table is cumulative: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\.resize\(n_attn_workers\)' HEAD -- h` marks per-forward tables, which are out of scope. Index expressions: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(note_attn_job|note_join_wait|add_visits|token_path_span|[^a-z_]row)\(' HEAD -- h`. Index definition: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'num_workers\(\) - n_attn_workers|Note \[Attention workers are the last' HEAD -- h/tron/models/model.hpp`. Per-forward dependence: `git -C WT grep -n 'recommend_n_main_helpers' HEAD -- h`. Sample sizes: `grep -n -E 'n_workers|active_workers' body.md`. Fold bounds: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp | grep -n -E 'for \(size_t w = 0; w < n_workers'`. Compare the exported leaf name (`<class>_worker_<W>`) with what the index means. The key-spelling comparison (`pool_worker(` versus the inline formula) belongs to the duplicate-logic check and runs only on a head that answers the row-key finding; at the reviewed head there is one spelling (self_attention.hpp:797).

5. Whole-forward predicates (d): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(\? [a-z_:]+_class::|\.size\(\) >= [a-z_]+_tokens|== [a-z_]+\.size\(\))'`; an `== x.size()` hit counts only when its result selects a bucket, a budget or a class, not a validator or an assert return. Body version: for a live review `gh pr view N --json body -q .body`; for a replay of a reviewed head `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:50){nodes{editedAt diff}}}}}'` and take the newest editedAt before the review timestamp; `grep -n -i -E 'runtron|rinzler|continuous batching'` on that text. Production batching: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp | grep -n -E 'compute_forward_args\(|while \(!stk\.empty\(\)\)|attempt_kv_job\(|ensure_listener\('` and read compute_forward_args: the stack walk over the token tree pushes a KV job per not-ready token of any user and a listener per node that needs logits, so one forward holds the union of all users' pending jobs. Per-element key: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'n_listeners = |in_listener_index|token_jobs\.size\(\)' HEAD -- h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp | grep -n 'stats_enabled ='`. Bucket definition: `git -C WT show HEAD:README.stats.md | grep -n -i 'decode_like'`. Write Insufficient data only for a scheduler outside full.hpp.

6. Report one finding per record, per subsystem, per table and per predicate, each with two remedies and, for a design question, a documentation fallback.

On PR 4596 (reviewed head 1430736b2a, BASE 66c7bb8db1): record forward_counters at h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:244-249 (forwards, wall_cycles, wall_max_cycles, fpga_queries, token_jobs, token_jobs_by_path_set); qualified grep gives writes at :439-441 (note_forward_wall, :436), :461 and :463 (end_forward, :447), :471 (note_fpga_query, :468), readers at :633-676; note_forward_wall called from h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2100-2103 around state.forward at :2096 (the only production state.forward caller in h, src, t); begin_forward (:357) and end_forward called from h/tron/models/model.hpp:1745-1750; note_forward_wall reads current_class (:438) that begin_forward stores (:359). Rows sized by attn.size() at h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:496-498 after attn.resize(app_pool().num_workers()) at :480, rows vector N_CLASSES_2 * n_workers * n_layers at attn_stats.hpp:312; indexed by worker_ix at self_attention.hpp:855 and :1315 and by scratchpad at :1652; pool thread of attention worker i = num_workers() - n_attn_workers + i (model.hpp:1721-1722, :2244-2251); n_attn_workers from recommend_n_main_helpers (model.hpp:1994); fold over all n_workers at attn_stats.hpp:526 and :575; body sample n_workers 27, active_workers 20. Predicate n_listeners == token_jobs.size() at model.hpp:1746, n_listeners = in_listener_index.size() at :1671; stats_enabled hoists at self_attention.hpp:804 and :1452; README decode_like at :246-248; compute_forward_args at full.hpp:2242, stack walk :2278, KV job :2383, listeners :2469 and :2478. The body version of 2026-09-25T22:31Z (last before the 2026-09-28 review) names runtron and not rinzler; the live body (2026-10-01) names both. Remedies taken at 8c95514924: forward_scope attn_stats.hpp:866-883 constructed at model.hpp:1735; pool_worker helper attn_stats.hpp:431 used at self_attention.hpp:855, :1343, :1485; n_attn_workers_max attn_stats.hpp:301; README.stats.md:252 at ae8a6d38d9 'So `decode_like` counts pure-decode forwards only.'

On PR 2176 (635de61895): if constexpr (head_size == 128 && n_kv_heads <= 32) at h/tron/models/model.hpp:773, gof_configure at :774-775; direct calls gof_on_save_k :1419-1420 and gof_on_save_v :1466-1467 with no guard; gof_n_layers is 0 before configure and after reset (src/tron/gof.cpp:53, :84); divisions by it at gof.cpp:191-192 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:814 (key / gof_max_layers()). Fix 8a6db72438 ('Address PR #2176 review feedback', 2026-03-18): `std::vector<kv_save_observer_t> on_save_k` declared at model.hpp:629, registered inside the guard at :784-786 and iterated at :1435; 348799cf1a adds on_flush_partial, on_await_dma and on_forward_poll the same way. At the later commit 8e19ea3e62 the whole registration block sits at :792-810 and the loops at :1453 and :1500.

Owned by other checks (PR 2287): 3029165954 (clear_kv_complete at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:560 at c459e255d9 with zero callers) is the dead-symbol check; 3029194687 (inline getenv("TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN") at model.hpp:820 at 4274d5878a beside fwd_hw_attn_enabled(), which reads USE_HW_ATTN at h/tron/models/hw_attn_config.hpp:19 and is used at model.hpp:1434 and self_attention.hpp:699; two variables gate one subsystem, Wade's ask was 'replaced with the fwd_hw_attn_enabled() function') is the duplicate-logic check.
final.widen_delta: The existing 13 checks never enumerate the writers of a record, the production callers of an inner function, the guards above every call into a gated subsystem, or the meaning of a cumulative table index across forwards. Check 10 greps callers only to bin hunks; check 6 compares a claim with its enforcing declaration; check 12 counts includers. This check adds a state-ownership pass over h/tron/models and h/tron/scheduler hunks: a writer table per published record (atomic writes to record members only, qualified by instance), a production-caller list for the inner and outer writer with a clearance rule (a second writer inside the first's caller clears), a guard per call into a configured subsystem (excluding the diff's own feature switch), size-versus-index per cumulative table, and one domain question on whole-forward classes validated only under runtron, read from the pre-review body version and from compute_forward_args. Reset partners with zero callers and gates or keys spelled two ways are handed to the dead-symbol and duplicate-logic checks. The SKILL.md description line needs four more phrases: state written from two layers, calls outside a subsystem's gate, cumulative row keys that change meaning between forwards, whole-forward classes validated only under runtron. The common setup needs the first-parent BASE rule for merged PRs (merge-base returns HEAD itself). 'Words used here' needs: rinzler (the serving program; continuous batching = users join and leave between forwards, so one forward can carry one user's prompt chunk next to other users' generated tokens), runtron (the command-line tool; prompt and decode forwards never mix), FUSE (the file system that exports counters as leaves), GOF (a 4-token group of K/V the FPGA path transfers), pool worker versus attention worker (the last n_attn_workers pool workers run attention), published record (a struct a reader folds, prints or exports as one unit).

quotes.quote: Any other caller of `state.forward(...)` (another scheduler, a test harness, a draft path) gives `forwards == 0` next to nonzero `token_jobs`. `note_forward_wall` also relies on `current_class` having been set by `begin_forward` inside the forward.
quotes.what_it_shows: The two-writer finding names future callers, not the one caller at HEAD, and the hidden dependency of one writer on state the other sets; the ask followed as 'Consider owning T1 inside run_forward ... or wrap begin/end/wall in one scoped helper'.

quotes.quote: If `n_attn_workers` changes between forwards, attention worker `W` maps to a different pool thread (`num_workers() - n_attn_workers + W`), so a per-worker row mixes cores over the run.
quotes.what_it_shows: The row-key finding is grounded in the index definition (the pool-thread formula from model.hpp) and states the consequence for cumulative rows; it was posed as 'Design question on row sizing' with two remedies and a fallback.

quotes.quote: Was per-forward granularity chosen on purpose? A per-q_batch class, or tagging each token job by whether it has a listener, looks nearly free: it could be hoisted once per `apply_page_range` call like `stats_enabled`.
quotes.what_it_shows: The classification finding is a question with a code-readable cheap alternative (the per-element key at the counting site) and ends with a documentation fallback; the author kept per-forward and Wade accepted.

quotes.quote: good point... if we are going to conditionally use the HW KV-tree/GoF stuff based on acceptable model parameters, we should be consistent. I think your original `kv_save_observer_t` was a pretty slick way to achieve that
quotes.what_it_shows: The gate finding: Wade endorses a bot's 'calls outside the configure guard' finding and prefers the indirection (callbacks registered inside the guard) as the gating mechanism; the author restored the observer pattern in 8a6db72438.

residual_risks: Trigger (a) fires on tron-2875 or tron-4353 only if an agent misreads a moved value as two writers; the do_not_fire clause names both PRs, but a new silent PR with a value moved between instances of one structure without a Note or TRON_ASSERT would still be a candidate until step 2 clears it.
Step 5's body-version read depends on the GraphQL userContentEdits field; a PR body never edited has no edit nodes, and the agent must then use the live body.

The classification question (d) still rests on a domain judgement (whether a whole-forward class misattributes most decode attention under rinzler); the procedure makes the mixed-forward fact readable from compute_forward_args, but the magnitude of misattribution is not readable from code. Insufficient data for that magnitude; a rinzler run with the stats enabled would resolve it.

The gate step (b) is written for the tron::hardware::gof_* namespace; another gated subsystem needs its namespace prefix substituted, and the unconfigured-behaviour read (divide by a configured count) is a pattern, not a grep.
n = 4 over 2 PRs is the smallest member set among the add_new items; the gate case rests on one reply endorsing a bot, and no second gate finding in Wade's own words exists in the corpus.
